solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       i.id,
       ROUND(AVG(i.amount) OVER (
         PARTITION BY s.customer_id
         ORDER BY i.issued_at, i.id
         ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ), 2) AS moving_avg
FROM invoices i
JOIN shipments s ON s.id = i.shipment_id
ORDER BY s.customer_id, i.issued_at, i.id;

rules.howSolved: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW gives each invoice and up to two earlier ones for the same customer. The first invoice averages only itself, and the second averages two.
ROUND(AVG(...), 2) rounds the average after it is computed.

ambiguities: 'Round the average to two decimal places' is read as PostgreSQL ROUND on numeric, which rounds exact halves away from zero. The precision dataset has two exact half-cent averages, and a round-half-to-even reading would round those two rows down, so the convention changes the result there. Sample and ties have no half-cent averages. The instruction says only 'round', so I used the standard half-up ROUND.
notes: Sample returns 205 rows, ties 154, precision 154. A correlated formulation that averages the last three rows explicitly gives 0 differences on all three datasets. The rounding convention is the only open point and affects 2 rows in the precision dataset.
